How accurate · Digital twin: one year, 495 wells

How accurate is it?

A forecast is only useful if it holds up when the answer isn't known yet. So we tested ours the honest way: pretend it is an earlier date, forecast from that point, then compare with what really happened.

How we tested

  1. Go back in time. We picked 8 dates between December 2025 and July 2026.
  2. Hide the future. At each date, the model saw only the readings up to that day.
  3. Forecast every well 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12 weeks ahead, about 3,600 forecasts per horizon.
  4. Check against reality. Measure how far off each forecast was.

We also ran an automatic check that scrambles all data after each test date. The forecasts did not change at all, which proves they never peeked at the future.

"Our forecast" blends the recent-trend view and the pumping + rain model. The mix was chosen at each test date using only earlier results.

Are the ranges honest?

Every forecast comes with an "80% likely" range. If that label is true, the real level should land inside the range about 8 times out of 10. It did.

One week ahead

Over a single week the water barely moves, so even "assume nothing changes" does well. Most of the remaining error is ordinary week-to-week wobble in the readings.

The very short term: each pumping session

A separate set of models predicts what happens during and just after each pump run. They are useful for spotting a session that will pull the water unusually deep.

Level when the pump next starts——

What this shows
  • Forecasts up to 12 weeks ahead beat simple guesses, and the gap grows with time.
  • Rainfall matters: it is what separates our forecast from "the trend continues".
  • The ranges mean what they say.
What is not proven yet
  • All of this is on a digital twin (simulated wells), not yet on years of real records.
  • We could not yet test forecasting through a monsoon: the year's only monsoon was needed to learn from.
  • Nothing beyond 12 weeks has been tested.

What we need to prove it on real wells →

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
